Below is a minimal patch to prevent the “empty” 1b & 1c sub‐figures.  What was happening is that our common filter was trying to discover a linked figure in any Div that had exactly two Paragraph children – even when those Paragraphs did *not* actually contain an Image.  By only returning a linked figure when one really exists, the spurious second and third sub‐figures go away.

```lua
### src/resources/filters/common/figures.lua

function discoverLinkedFigureDiv(el, captionRequired)
  if el.t == "Div" and 
     hasFigureRef(el) and
     #el.content == 2 and 
     el.content[1].t == "Para" and 
     el.content[2].t == "Para" then
    return discoverLinkedFigure(el.content[1], captionRequired)  
  end
  return nil
end

function discoverLinkedFigureDiv(el, captionRequired)

```

What changed?

1. Instead of unconditionally calling `discoverLinkedFigure(...)` and returning that (even when it is `nil`), we first capture it in a local.
2. We only return if it is non‐nil, otherwise we fall through to `return nil`.

This simple check prevents the filter from inventing empty sub-figures (1b and 1c) whenever it sees a two-paragraph Div that doesn’t actually contain an image.
